Cut the upper internal keyway through the bore lands; the larger register and rear taper naturally remove its ends.
features.justification: Section A-A shows the longitudinal keyway floor continuing from the register shoulder until it exits into the expanding rear bore. A full-length cutter gives precisely that visible extent; the cutter overshoots both end planes.

features.rationale: Produce the diametrically opposite internal keyway.

features.rationale: Confirm the angular location of the radial .500-13 hole relative to the bent section trace before orienting its radial drilling axis.
features.justification: 27/64 inch is the standard tap drill for 1/2-13 UNC. The drilling depth would break into the bore without reaching the opposite wall. The coordinates are a non-executable placeholder pending confirmation of clocking.

features.rationale: Mill the bottom rear retaining pocket, open to the tapered bore and semicircular at the screw end.
features.justification: The rear detail shows a semicircular end concentric with the retaining screw, tangent to the two parallel .501-wide sides; its radius is therefore D046/2. The other slot end lies wholly in the existing bore, overshooting the open inner boundary. The pocket seat depth is explicitly .625.

notes: This single-part plan covers detail 1, SB-12054-1. Details 4 (four retainers) and 5 (one insert) are separate parts, not bosses to fuse to detail 1. Their dimensions D051-D064 require separate part plans and separate frames; the supplied single-part IR has no component/assembly container.
Do not build unresolved or unsupported features. Their geometry fields are placeholders, not approved manufacturing definitions.
The front-face view is the -Z view, with its horizontal and vertical coordinates retained as global X and Y. Z=0 is the front register face; Z=D016 is the rear end.
Mounting-hole centers use D010-D012, including the rounded coordinate values. Do not force an exact sixfold circular pattern from the reference bolt-circle diameter.
Axial holes through the front flange use deliberately overshooting finite depths. A global thru cut would incorrectly perforate the rear flange.
D028 and D029 describe inspection balls and the measurement between them; neither is a chuck bore diameter or a component to add. Verify the finished taper against that inspection requirement.
The extracted D070 is rounded. Its controlling relation is (D030-D027)/(2*tan(D034 degrees)); use that relation at full precision in the dimensional environment.
D050 is not a printed radius. Rear-pocket semicircular end geometry is grounded in the rear view and modeled as D046/2, not as an independent measured dimension.

D065 is a carburized case-depth range, not a geometric cut. Detail 1 material is 4130 or 8630 steel; carburize and harden .030-.040 deep, grind wear surfaces to Rc58-62, other surfaces Rc40-45, temper at 350-400°F after quench.
Preserve datum A at the 5.5000 register, the front-face perpendicularity D066, and the bore/taper .0005 TIR requirements D067-D068 as inspection metadata.
Threads are cosmetic. The standard tap drills used here do not imply an unprinted thread fit class.
Confirm the faint title-block suffix before manufacturing release; the explicit part marking is SB-12054.
